docx.texto: How to build perfect prompts for the restaurant industry from scratch
Included with your Pro Prompts eBook · aichef.pro

80% of professionals who use AI in their food business don't get results because their prompts are too vague. "Give me ideas for my menu" or "help me with marketing" produce generic answers that are no use to anyone.
This guide teaches you the exact framework we use at AI Chef Pro to build prompts that deliver professional results from the very first query.
The 5 Elements of a Perfect Prompt
Act as an executive chef with 15 years of experience in contemporary Mediterranean cooking
My restaurant has 40 seats, a $45 average check, Southern cuisine, in a busy downtown neighborhood
Design a seasonal 4-course fall menu that uses local seasonal ingredients
(nothing — the AI makes up whatever is missing)
No shellfish. Maximum food cost 32%. Mise en place time per dish: 8 minutes max.
(nothing — you get whatever the AI decides)
Format: table with columns dish name / main ingredient / technique / suggested menu price

"Act as a chef with experience in seafood cooking. Create a sea bass recipe for a restaurant with a $35 average check in Charleston. Technique: low-temperature oven. No tree nuts. Format: dish name, ingredients for 4 servings with weights, step-by-step method, plating, suggested menu price."

"Calculate the food cost of this recipe [ingredient list with weights and price/lb]. Target selling price: $18. Give me: cost per ingredient, total ingredient cost, food cost %, and if it exceeds 30%, suggest 2 optimizations without lowering perceived quality."

"Write an Instagram post to launch our new seasonal dish: roasted butternut squash soup with a seared scallop and truffle oil. Elegant yet friendly tone. CTA: book a table. 150 words + 15 hashtags. My restaurant: Harbor Table, Boston, contemporary market-driven cuisine."
"Give me a menu for a wedding"

"Design the menu proposal for a 120-guest wedding at a countryside venue outside Austin, Texas, in June. Budget: $85 per person, excluding drinks. 8 vegan guests and 4 guests with celiac disease confirmed. Format: plated service, 3 courses. Include a welcome cocktail hour, the full menu with alternatives for dietary restrictions, and a staffing estimate."
Trigger Phrases That Improve Any Prompt
"Don't generalize, talk specifically about my case"
"Give me the executive summary first, then the details"
"Treat me like a professional chef with 10 years of experience"
"Explain it as if I had to implement it tomorrow"
"Now make it shorter and more direct"
"Give me 3 alternative variations of this proposal"

TEMPLATE 10 — Constructive feedback for your team
Full prompt (copy and paste into the AI)
e.g., cold station cook / front-of-house manager / pastry apprentice

I need to give feedback to [EMPLOYEE PROFILE] about this problem: [OBJECTIVE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION].

Context: they have been on the team for [TIME ON TEAM], and the impact on the business is [IMPACT DESCRIPTION].

Help me with:
1. How to open the conversation without causing defensiveness
2. The exact phrases to describe the problem (SBI model)
3. How to listen to their perspective
4. How to agree on a measurable improvement plan
5. How to close on a positive note
e.g., has been arriving 15-20 min late for 3 weeks without notice
e.g., delays mise en place and creates tension on the team

GOLDEN RULES for using prompts in the restaurant industry
1.  One prompt = one task. Don't mix goals in the same message.
2.  Always fill in the [PLACEHOLDERS]. The more specific you are, the better the result.
3.  If the answer isn't good, don't repeat the same prompt. Add more context.
4.  Putting the role at the start of the prompt improves quality by up to 40%.
5.  Always ask for the format you need: table, list, email, step by step.
6.  For deep analysis, use Perplexity or Claude with web search turned on.
7.  Save your best customized prompts. They are your most valuable asset.
